newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says 1996 GDP to be up 4.6-4.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says 1996 GDP to be up 4.6-4.7 pct.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Tuesday preliminary data showed 1996 gross domestic product rose 4.6-4.7 percent, and he predicted that inflation would drop below two percent in February.
Gross domestic product (GDP) "will definitely be between 4.6 and 4.7 percent up to the end of last year," he said during a tour of the central state of Queretaro.
He added that preliminary fourth quarter data showed industrial output up 5-6 percent, construction rebounding, and retail and wholesale sales recovering.
In a statement reporting Ortiz's comments, the Finance Ministry said he also predicted that inflation would be "slightly above two percent" in January.
"In February, there will be a substantial reduction, taking it below two percent, which will lead very positively to a reduction in interest rates," he added.

Referring to employment, Ortiz said workers permanently insured with the Mexican Social Security Institute number around eight million, above the level in December 1995 when Mexico was in the throes of financial crisis.
In the latest Reuters survey MXAAP, analysts expected 1996 GDP to rise 4.61 percent and January inflation to rise 2.18 percent.
